content: 1. Strong inducers of the CYP3A4 enzyme significantly reduce the systemic exposure of flibanserin, potentially decreasing its therapeutic efficacy. 2. Both nalbuphine and flibanserin can increase sedation when co-administered. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in such cases. 3. The risk of sedation is heightened when flibanserin is used alongside other central nervous system (CNS) depressants. 4. Flibanserin increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring for adverse effects is recommended when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 5. Nevirapine reduces the levels or effects of flibanserin by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Nifedipine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Co-administration of flibanserin with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may lead to increased adverse effects of flibanserin. 8. The interaction mechanism between flibanserin and olanzapine is unspecified, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. 14. Antipsychotics may enhance the serotonergic effects of serotonin modulators, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitoring for signs of serotonin toxicity (e.g., mental status changes, autonomic instability, neuromuscular hyperactivity) or neuroleptic malignant syndrome (e.g., hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, autonomic dysfunction) is essential. 15.
